one_liner: An Air Force direct-hire 'landing page' for Social Science (0101) jobs; it routes you to the Air Force Civilian Service Direct Hire Job Board rather than describing one specific job.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge and emergency-management consulting at IEM could fit some 0101 social science work, but this posting has no actual duties, qualifications, or job details to match against. The 0101 series normally requires a social science degree or a qualifying mix of coursework and experience, and nothing on file confirms Daniel has that. Treat this as a pointer to the real postings on the Direct Hire Job Board.
eligibility: Open to the public under Direct Hire Authority, so no prior federal status or veterans' preference is needed.

The posting lists no qualifications. Check whether the specific job on the Direct Hire Job Board requires a social science degree, or 24 semester hours of related coursework plus experience, which is typical for the 0101 series.
NH-1/4 is a pay-band range under the Acquisition Demonstration Project, and the grade you qualify for will depend on specialized experience shown in the actual announcement.
No security clearance is required according to this posting, but confirm this on the specific opportunity.
Location is negotiable after selection, with no telework or remote work, so expect to work on site wherever the job is placed.
strategy: Before applying, open the Air Force Civilian Service Direct Hire Job Board link and find the actual 0101 opportunity, because this posting contains no duties to tailor to.
Confirm your college degree major and coursework; if you have 24+ semester hours in social sciences, list them clearly or attach transcripts.

Frame your IEM work in social-science terms: research, analysis of disaster recovery or preparedness data, writing reports, and working with government stakeholders. Use only the duties you actually performed.
Keep the resume to two pages, and for each job list start and end dates (month/year), hours per week, and brief specialized-experience bullets.
Because the posting stays open until March 2027 and direct hire can move fast, apply early and keep your USAJOBS profile and documents ready.
In parallel, apply to postings with clearer duties that fit you better, such as FEMA or state and local emergency management or legislative-office roles.
resume_bullets: Analyzed [type of data/plans] for [government client type] on [disaster recovery/preparedness] projects at IEM, producing [reports/briefings] used to [decision or outcome].
Researched [policy/regulatory topic] and wrote [number] [memos/reports] summarizing findings for [audience], [hours/week], [dates].
Coordinated with [number/type] of federal, state, or local stakeholders to gather information and present recommendations on [topic].
interview_questions: Describe a research or analysis project you led from start to finish. What methods did you use?
How did your emergency-management consulting work involve social science research or analysis?
Tell us about a time you explained complex findings to a non-expert audience.
How do you handle working with stakeholders who have conflicting priorities?
watch_outs: This posting is a generic placeholder with no real duties or qualifications, so the real requirements are only on the linked job board.
The 0101 series usually has an education requirement, and you may not qualify without social science coursework.
The salary range is very broad and the location is unknown, and you would be expected to report on site wherever placed, possibly away from Northern Virginia.
